blocks.text:
Arrival at Rio de Janeiro Airport, where you will be met and transferred to your hotel. After check-in, the rest of the day is free. There are no scheduled activities on the first day, so you can recover from your flight and visit the oceanfront whenever you wish. This break is especially welcome before two full sightseeing days and the night at the Sambadrome.

Rio gradually reveals its contrasts along the drive. The road passes through tunnels, high-rise neighbourhoods rise against granite slopes, and the ocean appears around the bends. Long beaches, a major stadium, the Botanical Garden, mountains and densely built districts all share the same city.

After an international flight, there is no need to rush. Copacabana is ideal for a first stroll: walk along the water, listen to the surf, stop for fresh juice and watch daytime Rio turn into an evening city. The principal excursions and Carnival night are still ahead, so your first evening can remain entirely free while you prepare for the next day.

This first evening also helps you appreciate the scale of Rio. The beachfront runs beside dense city blocks, with hills rising immediately behind the buildings. Even without a guided tour, it is clear that nature is woven into the city rather than confined to its outskirts. The ocean, rocky peaks and green spaces appear between the streets, making even an ordinary airport transfer part of discovering Rio.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, set out on a tour of Sugar Loaf. The cable car first ascends to Morro da Urca. From its observation deck, enjoy views of the bay, yachts, the bridge to Niterói and city neighbourhoods nestled between rocky hills.

The second cable car takes you to the summit of Sugar Loaf. The panorama encompasses the beaches of Ipanema and Leblon, the Rio coastline, Guanabara Bay and Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado. From above, the remarkable proximity of the ocean, mountains and residential districts is especially clear.

After descending, explore the historic centre: monasteries, old churches, the Metropolitan Cathedral and colonial façades. The day reveals Rio at two scales: sweeping views over the bay and coastline in the morning, followed by individual streets and historic architecture.

Sugar Loaf and old Rio complement each other. From the summit, you see the curves of the beaches and the city’s overall geography; back at street level, the details come into focus. The historic quarter offers a closer look at the architecture, and the contrast between modern districts and old buildings becomes even more striking after the panoramic views.

Optional: dine on Brazilian meats at Fogo de Chão overlooking Sugar Loaf. Approximate cost: USD 75 per person.

Optional excursion: helicopter flight over Rio de Janeiro. The flight lasts approximately 10–30 minutes. Price: from USD 250.
